recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future desire for per-code external links should be handled as a new terminology design decision rather than inferred from this already-applied STU3 clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-16078 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 non-substantive FHIR-core clarification asking to add preferred HTTP specification links for the HTTP verb definitions on the HTTP verb CodeSystem page.
initial_application: The issue was applied as svn revision 14169, represented in git by f4da5602278eaa3576addcf3402cd8cf00b96a98. That commit added a markdown HTTP RFC link to the HTTPVerb description and changed the individual definitions from bare labels such as "HTTP GET" to sentence-style definitions such as "HTTP GET Command". Jira's application comment explains that links could not be embedded in each definition because the definition field is not markdown. Commit 86a07e2f5a18780ff44c6ef3daf33f0e6a85f066 later updated the link from RFC 2616 to RFC 7231.
additional_context: Bundle is active in source/fhir.ini, and Bundle.entry.request.method is required-bound to ValueSet/http-verb. Current CodeSystem/http-verb, ValueSet/http-verb, and the Bundle binding description all retain the RFC 7231 link. The tightly related FHIR-17092 issue about better HTTP verb definitions is already represented on the combined branch by commit 63bca72aa76ed1d2eb41bf001508df765ef3410d, so it was not republished here. Focused Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant FHIR-16078 discussion or conflicting decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current source already preserves the requested HTTP specification reference at the terminology description and binding-description level, while attempting per-concept markdown links would contradict the accepted application constraint.
